method_card.title: Mean, Median, Mode & Range
method_card.content:
In geography, you often need to summarise data sets using measures of central tendency (averages) and measures of spread.

Mean: Add all values together and divide by the number of values. Best for data without extreme outliers. Example: mean river width from 10 measurements.

Median: The middle value when data is arranged in order. If there's an even number of values, average the two middle ones. Best when data has outliers (extreme values won't distort it). Example: median house price in an area.

Mode: The most common value (or class). There can be no mode, one mode, or multiple modes. Best for categorical data. Example: the most common land use type in a survey.

Range: Highest value minus lowest value. Shows the spread of the data. A large range suggests high variability.

Interquartile Range (IQR): The range of the middle 50% of data (Q3 − Q1). Less affected by outliers than the range, so gives a better measure of typical spread.

When to use each: Mean for evenly spread data, median for data with outliers, mode for categorical/qualitative data, range for quick spread assessment.
method_card.example:
Question: A student recorded river widths (m) at 5 points: 2.3, 4.1, 3.5, 2.8, 3.3. Calculate the mean.

Step 1: Add: 2.3 + 4.1 + 3.5 + 2.8 + 3.3 = 16.0

Step 2: Divide by 5: 16.0 ÷ 5 = 3.2

Answer: Mean river width = 3.2m

gold.hint: Order all 12 values. Q1 = median of lower 6, Q3 = median of upper 6.
gold.display: A student collected river width data (m) at 12 sites: 2.1, 3.4, 2.8, 5.2, 3.1, 2.5, 4.8, 3.6, 2.9, 3.3, 4.1, 3.0. Calculate the IQR.
Two rivers were measured. River A: mean velocity 0.8 m/s, IQR 0.3 m/s. River B: mean velocity 1.2 m/s, IQR 0.9 m/s. Compare the rivers using both the average and the spread.
options: River B is faster on average but more variable; River A is slower but more consistent — suggesting a more uniform channel shape
River A is faster and more consistent
River B is faster and more consistent

misconceptions.message: Mean: B (1.2) > A (0.8) = faster flow. IQR: B (0.9) > A (0.3) = more variation. River A's smaller IQR suggests more uniform depth/width. River B's high IQR might indicate pools and riffles.

gold.display: A fieldwork team collected 20 temperature readings. The estimated mean from a grouped frequency table is 16.5°C, but the actual mean from raw data is 17.2°C. Why might these differ?
options: The estimated mean uses mid-points of class intervals, which may not match the actual distribution within each class
Grouped data always gives a higher mean

misconceptions.message: When estimating the mean from grouped data, we use mid-points. If actual values cluster near the top of each class, the true mean will be higher than the estimate.

gold.display: An environmental survey recorded CO₂ levels (ppm) at 10 sites near a factory: 380, 395, 410, 425, 1200, 390, 405, 415, 400, 385. Which average best represents typical conditions, and what is its value?
options: Median = 402.5 — the 1200 reading is an extreme outlier that would skew the mean
Mean = 480.5 — it includes all the data
Mode — it ignores all outliers completely
Range = 820 — it shows the full spread

misconceptions.message: Mean = 4805÷10 = 480.5, heavily skewed by the 1200 outlier. Ordered: 380,385,390,395,400,405,410,415,425,1200. Median = (400+405)/2 = 402.5 — better represents typical conditions.

gold.display: City A (coastal): mean = 12°C, range = 8°C. City B (inland): mean = 12°C, range = 22°C. Explain the geographical significance of these statistics.
options: Both have the same average but City B has much greater variation due to continentality — the sea moderates City A's temperatures
City B is hotter because it has a larger range
The range is irrelevant — only the mean matters
City A must be further from the equator because its range is smaller

misconceptions.message: Equal means but very different ranges = continentality. The sea (high specific heat capacity) moderates coastal City A. Inland City B has hot summers and cold winters.

bronze.display: A student recorded daily temperatures (°C) for a week: 14, 16, 13, 17, 15, 14, 12. Calculate the mean temperature. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

bronze.hint: Order the data from smallest to largest first.
bronze.display: River depths (m) measured at 7 points across a channel: 0.3, 0.8, 1.2, 1.5, 1.1, 0.7, 0.4. Find the median depth.
A land use survey recorded: residential, residential, commercial, residential, parkland, commercial, residential, industrial, residential. What is the modal land use?

misconceptions.message: Count each: residential = 5, commercial = 2, parkland = 1, industrial = 1. Mode = residential (most frequent).

bronze.display: Rainfall data (mm) for 6 months: 45, 38, 52, 41, 60, 35. Calculate the range.

misconceptions.message: Range = highest − lowest = 60 − 35 = 25mm.

bronze.display: Traffic counts at a junction: 120, 135, 128, 140, 135, 115, 135, 122. What is the mode?

misconceptions.message: 135 appears 3 times (more than any other value). Mode = 135 vehicles.

bronze.display: The bar chart shows tourist arrivals (thousands) per month. Calculate the mean number of monthly tourists.
Soil pH readings at 8 sites: 5.2, 6.1, 5.8, 5.5, 6.3, 5.2, 5.9, 5.2. What is the mode?

misconceptions.message: 5.2 appears 3 times, more than any other value. Mode = 5.2.

bronze.hint: With an even number of values, find the mean of the two middle values.
bronze.display: Wind speed data (km/h): 15, 22, 18, 25, 20, 12. Find the median wind speed.

misconceptions.message: Order: 12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25. Two middle values: 18 and 20. Median = (18+20) ÷ 2 = 19 km/h.

silver.hint: Multiply each size by its frequency, sum the products, then divide by total frequency.
silver.display: A student measured pebble sizes (cm) on a beach. The bar chart shows the results. Calculate the mean pebble size.
Temperature readings (°C) at noon for 10 days: 18, 22, 15, 20, 45, 19, 21, 17, 20, 18. The median is more appropriate than the mean. What is the median?

misconceptions.message: Order: 15,17,18,18,19,20,20,21,22,45. 10 values → median = (19+20)÷2 = 19.5°C. The 45°C outlier skews the mean but not the median.

silver.hint: Order the data. Q1 = median of lower half, Q3 = median of upper half. IQR = Q3 − Q1.
silver.display: River velocity data (m/s) at a downstream site: 0.8, 1.2, 0.9, 1.5, 1.1, 1.3, 0.7, 1.0. Calculate the interquartile range (IQR).
A grouped frequency table shows heights of vegetation: 0-10cm: 8, 10-20cm: 15, 20-30cm: 12, 30-40cm: 5. Which class interval is the modal class?

misconceptions.message: The modal class has the highest frequency. 10-20cm has 15 plants — the most of any class.

silver.display: Two beaches were surveyed. Beach A pebble sizes: mean = 4.2cm, range = 8. Beach B: mean = 4.0cm, range = 3. Which beach has more consistent pebble sizes?
options: Cannot tell from mean and range alone

misconceptions.message: Smaller range = less variation = more consistent. Beach B (range 3) has pebbles of more similar sizes than Beach A (range 8).

silver.display: Monthly rainfall data (mm): 45, 38, 42, 55, 62, 48, 50, 44, 52, 40, 58, 46. Calculate the mean rainfall to the nearest whole number.
A geographer measures temperature at 6 sites: 12°C, 14°C, 11°C, 13°C, 14°C, 14°C. Calculate the mean, median and mode.

worked_examples.question: Temperature data for a week: 12, 14, 11, 15, 13, 18, 14. Find the median and range.

steps.label: Compare
steps.content: The mean (63) is pulled up by the outlier (150). The median (49) better represents the typical count. Use median when outliers are present.
